title: MB1-02575
frame:
Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: On December 10, 2012, the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) received an application to reopen the refugee protection claim of XXXX XXXX, a citizen of Egypt, in accordance with rule 55 of the Refugee Protection Division Rules (RPD Rules). This application follows the RPD decision rendered on November 30, 2012, declaring the abandonment of her refugee protection claim. A notice of decision was sent to the applicant on December 4, 2012.
The RPD Rules were amended on December 15, 2012; as a result, this application will be analyzed in accordance with rule 62 of the new RPD Rules.

The RPD's jurisdiction to reopen refugee protection claims is very limited. Subrule 62(6) of the RPD Rules states that the application to reopen must not be allowed unless it is established that there was a failure to observe a principle of natural justice.

In this respect, case law1 states that once the RPD has rendered a decision, it has discharged its duty (functus officio) and cannot exercise it a second time in the same case, unless there was a violation of the rules of natural justice.
The Minister responded to the application to reopen on December 18, 2012, and opposes this reopening, alleging that there was no failure to observe a principle of natural justice.

To support her application to reopen, the applicant submitted an affidavit dated December 10, 2012, in which she states that she did not receive the notice to appear for her hearing on November 15, 2012. She also did not receive the notice to appear for the abandonment hearing set for November 30, 2012, but she states that she received, at her new address, the notice of decision concerning the abandonment of her refugee protection claim, submitted under P-4.

The applicant explained that she had been living at her daughter's home until XXXX 2012. On XXXX XXXX, 2012, she allegedly had an argument with her daughter and son-in-law, and they allegedly forced her to leave the home. She stated that she filed a complaint about this with the police. However, the panel notes that no police report on this matter accompanies the affidavit.

The applicant stated that she stayed one night in a shelter and that the next day she allegedly went to stay at the home of people from her church. On XXXX XXXX, 2012, the priest at that church allegedly helped her find housing. The applicant submitted a letter from him under P-2. The panel notes that he states that he met Ms. XXXX (the applicant) for the first time on XXXX XXXX, 2012, that she spoke to him about the problems that she allegedly had with her daughter and son-in-law, and that she had no place to go. At that point, he allegedly took her to the home of a family, and she stayed there until he found her an apartment, on XXXX XXXX, 2012. A lease was signed on XXXX XXXX, 2012, and submitted with this application under P-3. The panel notes a minor discrepancy between the facts related by the applicant in her affidavit and what the priest stated in his letter-according to the applicant, she went to stay with people from the church on XXXX XXXX, 2012.

The applicant stated that she notified social assistance of her change of address in order to continue to receive her social assistance cheques. She stated that her daughter had been helping her with her refugee protection claim and, therefore, she did not know how to communicate with her lawyer or with Citizenship and Immigration Canada.

The panel is puzzled by this allegation because the Minister indicates in the Minister's response that the applicant notified the Minister of her change of address on XXXX XXXX, 2012-a copy of the notice was submitted under M-1. The panel notes that the applicant indicates on that notice that her new address is XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, XXXX XXXX, and that her previous address was XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, while the RPD had XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX, as her former address. Moreover, the Minister noted this and indicates in paragraph 10 of the Minister's response that the applicant had not yet provided CIC with her change of address; to this effect, the Minister submitted M-2, a printout from the Field Operations Support System (FOSS) that shows that, on XXXX XXXX, 2011, the applicant was living at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX, and that, on XXXX XXXX, 2012, her new address was XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX. There is no record of her stay at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX.

The Minister also points out that there is no explanation for the steps that the applicant allegedly took to try to communicate with her counsel after she moved or for the steps that her counsel allegedly took to try to communicate with the applicant.

The panel notes that the claimant allegedly moved to XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, on XXXX XXXX, 2012. She provided social assistance with her change of address on XXXX XXXX, 2012 (see P-3 submitted with this application). She provided CIC with her change of address on XXXX XXXX, 2012, (M-1) despite the allegation in her affidavit that she did not know how to communicate with CIC. In addition, the panel notes that, after receiving the notice of decision sent on December 4, 2012, to her correct address, the applicant did not explain how, at that point, she was able to communicate with her lawyer very quickly, because an application to reopen was received by the RPD on December 10, 2012. Neither the name nor the contact information of her counsel appears on that notice of decision (see P-1 submitted with this application).

Subrule 4(3) of the RPD Rules states that a claimant must provide their new contact information in writing to the RPD and to the Minister as soon as it changes. This rule is also clearly indicated on form IMM-5292,2 which was given to the applicant when she submitted her refugee protection claim, that is, that the applicant must provide her mailing address in writing to the RPD and to the Minister and that, as soon as her contact information changes, she must provide it in writing to the RPD and to the Minister. In addition, according to the evidence submitted by the Minister, the applicant provided the Minister with her change of address on XXXX XXXX, 2012, that is, before the notice to appear for the applicant's first hearing had been mailed. The applicant also should have provided her new contact information to the RPD. The panel notes that XXXX months passed between when she moved on XXXX XXXX, 2012, and her first hearing set for November 15, 2012. She allegedly had sufficient time, despite the shock of the move, to take the necessary steps to communicate with the RPD, either on her own or with the help of the church priest.

After reviewing the application to reopen, the Minister's response and the applicant's entire file, the panel is of the opinion that the evidence submitted does not demonstrate that there was a failure to observe the principles of natural justice. The notices to appear were sent to the applicant, to the address that the Board had on file. The applicant provided the Minister with her change of address on XXXX XXXX, 2012, but failed to provide her change of address in writing to the RPD, as required under rule 4; this does not constitute a failure to observe a principle of natural justice but rather a fact that may be attributed to her and for which she alone is responsible.

For these reasons, the application to reopen is dismissed.
